title: 機械材料Ⅰ
subtitle: Engineering materials I
educationalGoal: In this course, we will give an overview of the industrial materials and learn the basics of the relationship between structure and physical and chemical properties, as well as methods for evaluating the characteristics of materials.
advice:
The outline of the class is as follows:

Classification of machine materials and characteristics of metals, plastics, and ceramics
Structure of materials
Basics of crystallography
Theoretical strength and crystallographic dislocations in materials, resolved shear stress, and dislocation and deformation of a single crystal
Plastic deformation of materials
Materials evaluation, tensile test, stress versus strain curves, and hardness test
Phase transition of metals
books:
Textbooks: Mechanical Materials(3rd edition), Tokyo Denki University Press (in Japanese)
Reference books: None
Reserved books: Introduction Structure and Properties of Metallic Materials, Taiga Publishing Co., Ltd. (in Japanese)
requiredKnowledge:
Understand the basics of trigonometric functions, exponential functions, logarithmic functions, and vectors.
Memorize the elemental symbols, such as those for carbon, magnesium, aluminum, titanium, iron, and copper, related to materials science.
Regarding material structure, it is desirable to have knowledge of high school chemistry.

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain basic characteristics of metals, plastics, and ceramics.
Be able to explain types, features, and examples of atomic bonds.
Be able to explain the basics of crystallography (especially Bravais lattice and Miller index).
Be able to explain the difference between elastic and plastic deformation based on materials science.
Be able to explain basics of materials evaluation.
Be able to explain the relationship between equilibrium phase diagram and phase formation.

achievementLevels.ideal:
1: Explain the relationship between typical practical materials and specific applications.
2 & 3: Explain the crystal structure and physical and chemical characteristics of typical pure materials.
4: Explain the phenomena caused by elastic or plastic deformation (for example, slip and twinning deformation) using a crystallographic viewpoint.
5: Propose an appropriate material evaluation test method.
6: Explain phase rate and microstructure at a particular point.
achievementLevels.standard:
1: Explain the characteristics used to measure practical materials and their physical properties (such as Young’s modulus and melting point).
2: Explain the bond types in pure substances and their characteristics.
3: Illustrate crystal planes and directions.
4: Explain the deformation process of mild steel using the stress versus strain curve.
5: Explain material evaluation test methods (for example, tensile test and hardness test) and data processing.

lessons.content:
Lecture:
Learn the classification of substances, the
type s and characteristics of atomic bonds of
the atoms that make up substances, and related
properties.
lessons.assignments:
Review the crystal structure
of pure substances, such as
Au, Al, Fe, and Mg.
Study Japanese Industrial
Standards (JIS) G3101,
G4051, G4401, G5501, and
H4000.
Understand characteristics of
the materials discussed
in the standards.

lessons.content:
Lecture:
Learn basics of crystallography, difference
between single crystals and polycrystals,
and calculation of the theoretical density
of pure substances.
lessons.assignments:
Review the typical crystal
structures of pure metals.

lessons.content:
Quiz 1:
Check the level of understanding of lectures
from classes 1-3.

Lecture:
Learn unit cell, space lattice, Miller index,
atomic packing factor, and related concepts.
lessons.assignments:
Review the content of classes
1-3 to prepare for Quiz 1.

lessons.content:
Self-reflection class:
Return Quiz 1 and review answers.

Lecture:
More on unit cell, space lattice, and Miller
index.
lessons.assignments:
After review the quiz, create
and submit a self-checking
sheet and consider your
future study plans.

Review the exercises for
understanding unit cell and
Miller index.

lessons.content:
Lecture:
Learn perfect crystals, the types and features
of lattice defects, difference between elastic
deformation and plastic deformation, and
difference between slip deformation and
twinning deformation.
lessons.assignments:
Review the slip systems of BCC
and FCC crystals.

lessons.content:
Lecture:
Learn the basics of material evaluation tests.
Learn technical terms that represent
mechanical properties of materials.
lessons.assignments:
Study JIS G0202, Z2241,
Z2242, Z2243-1, and Z2244.
Study the differences between
materials evaluation tests.

lessons.content:
Lecture:
Learn material testing to evaluate the
strength of materials that are essential for
the design
of machine structures.

Quiz 2:
Check the level of understanding of the
lectures
from classes 4-8.

Lecture:
Learn basics of the microstructure controls,
difference between pure metal, solid solution,
and alloy.
Learn technical terms for microstructure
control, for example, crystallization,
precipitation, and phase transformation.
lessons.assignments:
Review the content of classes
4-8 to prepare for Quiz 2.

lessons.content:
Self-reflection class:
Review Quiz 2 and its answers.
As needed, review previous lectures to answer
questions and reinforce knowledge.

and submit a self-checking
sheet and consider your
future study plans.

Review the content of classes
1-8.
Review technical terms of
microstructure control.

lessons.content:
Lecture:
Learn the relationship between equilibrium
phase diagrams and microstructure.

Quiz 3:
Check the level of understanding of lectures
from classes 9-11.

Integrated learning:
Discuss the characteristics of materials
expecte d to be developed in the future and
their application fields.
lessons.assignments:
Review the content of classes
9-11 to prepare for Quiz 3.
